factsAccepted: Technician billable utilization is 58% against a 70-75% industry benchmark, and revenue per truck fell from $430k pre-rollup to $367k (top-quartile operators reach ~$525k). The same trucks and technicians are producing materially less billable output post-rollup, indicating capacity is being lost in scheduling/dispatch rather than in demand or pricing.

Three of six acquired branches still run their original, separate dispatch/field-service software, with no unified scheduling or cross-branch capacity view. There is no normalized branch-level KPI scorecard, so dispatch efficiency (jobs/tech/day, drive-time, idle hours) cannot be compared across branches. This is a structural integration gap that prevents the platform from balancing load and enforcing scheduling discipline.

Consolidated revenue grew 52% YoY but organic same-branch revenue grew only 3%, while EBITDA margin fell from 13% to 9.5% (-350bps). Growth is almost entirely acquired, and profitability per dollar of revenue is deteriorating — the platform is getting bigger but less efficient, consistent with integration drag rather than healthy organic scaling.

Membership/maintenance-plan attachment varies extremely by branch: platform branches at 41% of customers, two acquired branches under 12%. Plan members provide recurring demand, demand-smoothing across shoulder seasons, and higher replacement-lead conversion. Low-attachment branches therefore have lumpier demand and lower utilization — but plan attachment is an operational discipline, not a demand-quality problem.
